{{< include ../_setup.qmd >}}

```{python}
d = aea.filter(pl.col("year") == LAST, pl.col("gas") == "GHG", pl.col("activity").is_in(ACTS)).group_by("activity").agg(pl.col("kt_co2_eq").sum())
total = d["kt_co2_eq"].sum(); hh = d.filter(pl.col("activity") == "HH")["kt_co2_eq"].sum()
ind = read("aea_indicators").filter(pl.col("year") == LAST, pl.col("activity") != "HH")
```

## Key figures {.theme-content}

- Emissions of resident units in `{python} LAST`: **`{python} mt(total)` Mt CO2 eq**.
- Households: **`{python} pct(hh / total)`** of the total.
- Intensity of the economy: **`{python} num(1000 * ind["ghg_kt"].sum() / ind["value_added_mtnd"].sum(), 0)` t CO2 eq** per million TND of value added.

## Dissemination

- Excel workbooks in three languages: accounts by activity and gas, bridge table, source by activity, indicators.
- The format follows the Eurostat questionnaire, which eases international comparison [@eurostat2015aea].
- Methods document and data explorer on the website.

## Points to discuss

- Joint release with the inventory, or with the national accounts?
- Which intensities to publish: per output, per value added, per household spending?
- Revision policy when the inventory or the national accounts are revised.
